name: ANSI/IEEE phase-angle meter symbol
summary: IEEE-library form of the phase meter, used where a drawing must show where the angle between two measured quantities is read.
description: In IEEE-oriented panel schematics the phase meter appears as a circular instrument fed from both a voltage reference and a current or second voltage input. The reading is the angle between those two inputs, so the symbol only makes sense when both connections are traced back to their instrument transformers and their polarity marks.

The circle and label identify an indicating instrument, not a protection function. It does not tell you the reference convention (leading or lagging positive), the frequency range or whether the meter is analogue or a digital display; those come from the instrument schedule and the vendor data.
readingNotes: Confirm which voltage is the reference and which quantity is compared against it.
Check CT and VT polarity dots, because a reversed input shifts the reading by 180 degrees.
drawingChecklist: Show polarity of the compared input
State the scale or angle convention
distinction: A phase-angle meter reads an angle; a power-factor meter reads the cosine of that angle and is scaled lead/lag around unity.
